meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, Hale. Turnitin's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have it printed in my bag. What else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I've got them. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Turn it closer. A wrong quotation is a careless seventeen-year-old, not proof of anything. And whatever comes of this, none of it goes on his record, and none of it gets around his class.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what an outline is for. And you skipped my point about the quotation.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Five minutes, put on the spot by a teacher he tells me has had it in for him since September. So where is this going?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at home. You've shown me five things and proposed nothing.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and it's marked well before his December 1 deadline. Nothing on his record, and nobody in that class hears a word.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday after school, marked within two days. Put the date and the time in tonight's email.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes, marked within two days. I'll be watching for that email tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that rewrite to be marked within two days, kept away from his class, and confirmed with its date and time in writing. I expect that written confirmation from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight and the rewrite marked within two days; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her 4:40 call.
What moved her: When she said he might have drafted it elsewhere and pasted it in, you invited Owen to show that other document and its history, which turned her defence into something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score and saying the zero stands gave her a machine's number she could dismiss with the vendor's own warning, and it cost you your first turn.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's creation at 11:31 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, with the text arriving at 11:52 and 11:58 PM, which came very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she called the invented Hamlet line mere carelessness, answer it on the spot by pointing out that a careless student misremembers a real line while this one does not exist anywhere in the play, rather than moving to your next document and letting her say you skipped it.
